newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan first-quarter GDP up 6.83 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan first-quarter GDP up 6.83 pct yr/yr.

text.p: Taiwan's gross domestic product grew 6.83 percent year-on-year in the first quarter, well above the fourth quarter's 6.62 percent annual rise, an official of the government's statistics agency said on Friday.
The dramatic first-quarter rise sharply surpassed an average forecast for a 6.48 percent increase that resulted from a May 12 Reuters Poll of Taiwan economists.
The figure far outstripped even the two most recent forecasts of the official statistics agency itself, the Directorate General of Budget, Accounting and Statistics.

The agency's most recent official forecast, issued in February, said first-quarter growth was on track to come in at 6.40 percent. A directorate official informally upgraded that forecast to 6.6 percent in late April.

Directorate economists attributed the big jump in growth chiefly to sharply higher turnover in the island's stock market, whose main index surged by some 25 percent in the first quarter. The index has been in a correction in April and May.
"The active stock market trading led to growth in the service sector," the agency said in an official statement.

The huge profits generated by the stock market fuelled a strong 6.6 percent year-on-year rise in consumer spending, which in turn contributed to a 8.1 percent expansion of the service sector, it said.

Despite the surprise first-quarter surge, the directorate revised downward its full-year 1997 GDP growth forecast to 6.24 percent from 6.28 percent, saying a devastating farm epidemic that erupted on March 20 would pull second-quarter growth sharply below original projections.

An islandwide outbreak of hog foot and mouth disease has forced Taiwan temporarily to ban all fresh and frozen pork exports -- a US$1.55 billion a year industry -- and to slaughter nearly four million of the island's 14 million hogs.

Agency director Wei Duan said full-year growth also would be negatively affected by a perceived breakdown in law and order in Taiwan, saying this was expected to slow investment due to eroding business confidence.
"The deteriorating social order will have a psychological impact on investment willingness," Wei told reporters after the GDP figures were released.
Wei issued the first official GDP forecast for 1998, saying Taiwan's economy was expected to grow 6.26 percent on the basis of current projections.
Taiwan's economy has slowed significantly from its "Asian dragon" days of double-digit growth in the 1980s.

Growth in the mid-1990s has hovered around six percent year but dipped 5.4 percent in second half of 1995 -- a time of intense political and military tensions with longtime arch rival communist China.

Helped by a range of government stimulus plans and an easing of frictions with China, GDP growth moved back above six percent in the second half of 1996, but still came in at a disappointing 5.71 percent for all of 1996.

The fourth quarter of 1996 showed a promising 6.62 percent year-on-year rise, prompting officials to announce that a solid recovery was under way -- a belief that was substantiated further by the strong first-quarter 1997 result.
"The trend of recovery is getting ever clearer," the agency statement said on Friday.
GDP growth (pct) 6.83 6.62 5.12
